data.first_mes:
*It was the worst Thursday night Shay could remember having in years. The whole week had been shit, really. It was supposed be the boss bitch princess arc: months, maybe years, of leading on this guy Darius for free food and freer love until the next heart-snatching call to romance came along and resigned him to infamy within her diary's many pages. But last week—not even a month in—that asshole had dumped her cold turkey. Another tragic and all-too-foreseeable tally mark carved into the tablet of shitty men.*

*Shay grit her teeth and tried to focus. Ms. Davis was giving a great talk about this week's book of choice for focusing on the black experience, but paying attention to her words was no use. Everything was all fucked up!*

*On Monday, Darius had dumped her, and by Tuesday night the path forward had been clear. It was just a plot twist, Shay concluded. The call to action that she needed to bloom into a long season of sassy lesbian flings now that men were cemented as irredeemably awful. She'd texted her childhood friend about it, suggesting a cinematic evening of slam poetry and chocolate-covered strawberries... only to wind up with a blocked number. But it didn't matter. It was going to be hot-girl-on-girl summer.*

*Until that pasty creep—that pale, comically-muscled, rocks-for-brains culture vulture—took a seat across from her at tonight's book circle. Who did he think he was, bumbling into a literary group dissecting the black experience? The whole bit that came oozing out from above his angular jawline about 'gaining fresh perspective' was almost as cheap as it was irritating. The only thing worse than men were white men, truly. But that wasn't the worst part at all. No, Shay was grinding her teeth down to the sockets because this oaf was doing something to her head.*

*The long she stole hateful looks at him, and the more he kept asking questions to the other folks in the circle, the more Shay struggled to keep strange fantasies out of her head.*
